plan: Given my private value of $10, I will bid conservatively to avoid overpaying. Bidding above my value could lead to a net loss since the prize is only worth $10 to me. I will bid slightly above half my value to increase the chance of winning while minimizing the risk of paying too much. This strategy aims to maximize profit by winning only when the third-highest bid is significantly lower than my value.

Given my private value of $30, I aim to bid below this to ensure profit if I win. I will bid slightly above the midpoint between $0 and $30 to balance risk and reward. This strategy considers that bidding too high risks paying close to my value, minimizing profit. I will bid $20, as it allows room for profit even if the third-highest bid is close to my bid. This approach maximizes potential profit while minimizing risk, as the values are independently drawn each round.

Given my private value of $25, I aim to maximize profit by bidding below my value to ensure a positive net gain if I win. I will bid strategically to outbid the third-highest bid while avoiding overpaying. I will bid $20 to leave a margin for profit, as winning with a bid higher than $25 would potentially result in a loss. This bid aims to balance winning chances with profitability, assuming other bids may range widely.
